stories.title: US Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq fall as softer producer prices and Fed tightening outlook weigh
stories.summary: On Friday, November 13 2026, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 192.16 points (‑0.37%) to 52,104.93, the S&P 500 dropped 73.80 points (‑0.97%) to 7,518.60, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 367.05 points (‑1.45%) to 24,999.04. The decline followed October producer‑price data that showed a moderated month‑over‑month increase but a 6.5% year‑over‑year rise—the strongest since November 2022—and remarks from Boston Fed President Susan Collins that additional rate hikes are likely, pushing two‑year Treasury yields toward their biggest weekly jump in two years.
stories.why: The move underscores how U.S. inflation data and Fed policy expectations can shift risk appetite and capital flows, which matters for Indian investors tracking global market sentiment.

stories.title: SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions
stories.summary: Witness its $30 billion bet on OpenAI in early 2025 or its announcement in February that its SB Energy subsidiary would spend $33 billion on a 9.2-gigawatt natural gas power plant. Starting about two years ago, SoftBank reportedly put down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.

stories.title: India's gold imports plunge 62.57% to $5.51 billion in October as prices fall below $4,000/oz
stories.summary: India's gold imports fell 39.9% to $24.78 billion during April-October 2026, down from $41.24 billion a year ago, according to Commerce Ministry data. October imports plunged 62.57% year-on-year to $5.51 billion amid a correction in global gold prices.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: Pro-government forces take Mekelle, residents report hardship
stories.summary: Within two weeks of the war’s start, pro-government troops entered Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region, and the city is now under national army control. Salon owner Firut Me’ar says residents are struggling to meet basic needs, with little money, low morale and almost no business, describing daily life as far from normal despite the change in control.
stories.why: Shows how the conflict’s rapid advance is affecting civilians in a major regional centre.

stories.title: US Defence Secretary presents medal to Arlington guard after protocol breach
stories.summary: A video from a Veterans Day ceremony showed Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, his wife and senior advisers laughing and posing in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before a guard asked them to be quiet. The Pentagon later announced that Hegseth awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal for his duties at the Tomb. Photos posted on the secretary’s X account show the presentation with members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment (the Old Guard).
stories.why: It illustrates the Pentagon’s response to a high‑profile breach of ceremony protocol at a national memorial.
